analysis.title: GS U.S. Industrials & Materials rates multis into Q3 autos & indu tech 6 Oct 2026
key_insights: The desk expects Q3 for industrial multis to set up like the broader Q3. Y/y order growth accelerated in Q1 and stepped up again in Q2, but Middle East escalation, high oil and rising rates mean orders could slow y/y in Q3.

Desk Q3 setup for multis: organic growth should accelerate and topline should beat consensus. Rising inflation and price/cost dynamics, flagged unanimously during conference season, could pinch margins. The result is in-line-ish earnings growth, and the open question is whether that gets bought or sold.
Positioning map across industrials. Well owned: JCI, AME, NVT, ITT, INIO. Underowned: VRT, LII, CARR, WSO, OTIS, IR. Debated: EMR, MMM, RRX, LECO, TT.

The desk tactically likes ETN: end markets span data center and other areas, the CFO is slowly setting expectations and beating them, the stock lagged key peers until recently, and positioning looks light after long-term money left over the last few years.

GIR (Mark Delaney) is more positive on fundamentals for Industrial Tech than for Autos. Industrial Tech is helped by growing datacenter capex and a broad industrial recovery, but the bar for stocks to trade higher is high, as it was after 2Q reports.

Heading into 3Q26 earnings, the median stock in GIR's Autos and Industrial Tech coverage is down 5% since 2Q26 results and down 4% YTD. Auto-exposed names are down 5% since earnings and 6% YTD, while Industrial Tech names are up 9% since 2Q results and 30% YTD at the median.

GIR expects traditional auto tier 1 suppliers to report results and guidance in line to below consensus. Global light vehicle production is tracking the low-single-digit y/y decline suppliers assumed, but weak China retail sales and Chinese OEM share gains abroad make demand harder for some suppliers.
GIR sees rising input costs, including memory, as a margin headwind for auto suppliers. It is lowering estimates and/or price targets for APTV, VC, BWA, VGNT, LEA and GNTX.

In Industrial Tech, GIR is particularly positive on APH and KEYS, citing datacenter capex plus A&D and industrial strength and attractive margins and FCF. It is also positive on FLEX (SOTP valuation support, with the 3QCY26 report possibly leaving long-term details for the November investor event) and constructive on SMID names ST and BDC, though it expects in-line results from those two given small datacenter exposure.
GIR is raising estimates and price targets for APH, KEYS and TEL to reflect datacenter capex growth.

Privo on risk: AI is the cleanest part of the setup. Inference demand looks durable, hyperscalers benefit, and compute is still short, with B200/H200 pricing as the real-time evidence. The view sees upside asymmetry for the low-breadth market into earnings, and a risk that weak macro with strong micro suddenly broadens the rally.

Pre-market tone: S&P futures up 25bps led by cyclicals, AI/data center names bid on Google nearing a nuclear energy deal with Constellation, Japan up 105bps, France and Germany up 70-80bps. Germany factory orders missed badly.
Commodities and rates this morning: WTI down 200bps to below $88, Brent below $99, corn approaching $5, European gas up 4% to $77, 10-year at 5.28% off yesterday's highs, DXY at $102.
RPM reports shortly and starts industrials and materials earnings. It saw heavy volume and a sharp sell-off into yesterday's close that drew debate.

Company items: Berkshire bought another 2.4mm LEN shares though LEN was very weak yesterday. LCID posted Q3 deliveries of 3.806 and production of 2,954 as part of a planned inventory reduction. TRN commented on an antidumping and countervailing duty petition on railway tank car imports from Mexico.

earnings_insights: Desk expects Q3 industrial multis to show an organic growth acceleration and a topline beat versus consensus, with margins pinched by price/cost. Earnings growth is expected roughly in line with consensus (estimate, not yet reported).
GIR expects Q3 results and guidance from traditional auto tier 1 suppliers to be in line to below consensus (preview, nothing reported yet).
GIR expects Industrial Tech Q3 results to resemble 2Q, with mostly strong results and guidance but a high bar for the stocks (preview). It expects ST and BDC to report in-line results and guidance.
LCID Q3 deliveries were 3.806 and production 2,954, as reported yesterday. The company is focused on planned inventory reduction as part of a reset targeting $1.4bn of cash improvements in 2026.
RPM reports pre-market 10/6/26 and APOG also reports pre-market 10/6/26. DAL reports pre-market 10/9/26.
